text:
julia.peopleops: quick question - an employee on unpaid parental LOA waived benefits at open enrollment and is returning 2024-07-15. They want coverage reinstated effective 7/15 with no gap. What's our process for LOA-return re-enrolls and backdating? Any limits on backdating, proration, and payroll catch-ups?
samuel.lee: Process: employee files a QLE (LOA return) within 30 days of return. People Ops submits HRIS transaction `LOA_RETURN_REENROLL` with requested `effective_date`. Carrier acceptance of retroactive effective dates varies. We need LOA approval memo + signed QLE + dependent docs if applicable.
julia.peopleops: so carrier rules decide if we can backdate. If carrier allows retro, payroll collects missed employee premiums?
samuel.lee: yes. If carrier accepts retro (some up to 60 days), benefits team sets effective_date to requested date and payroll posts catch-up. If carrier denies retro, coverage starts when carrier processes enrollment and gap remains.
hris-bot: System note: transaction type `LOA_RETURN_REENROLL`. System max backdate request = 60 days. Required attachments: LOA approval, signed QLE, dependent proof for additions.
payroll-bot: Payroll note: we can run a one-time catch-up deduction if we receive `effective_date`, `benefit_code`, and `employee_premium_amount` before payroll cutoff (T-5 business days). Optionally we can spread the catch-up over N pay periods. Tax treatment: medical deductions are pre-tax; retro withholdings may have state implications. Sample payload to include in ticket body:
```
benefit_code: MED_PREM
effective_date: 2024-07-15
employee_premium_amount: 124.50
payroll_action: one_time_catchup
```
anna.manager: Confirming employee Maya Torres returns 7/15 and wants to re-add spouse coverage. LOA docs and signed QLE attached.
julia.peopleops: A couple follow-ups: 1) HSA - can we retro deposit employer contribution and do catch-up payroll for employee HSA deductions? 2) Dependent care FSA - is retro funding allowed?
samuel.lee: HSA: typically yes, if plan permits and employee was eligible during retro months; watch annual contribution limits. Employer contributions can be posted retro if vendor supports. FSA: dependent care FSA rarely allows retro funding for prior pay periods; health FSA depends on vendor. Recommend vendor confirmation.
hris-bot: Reminder: add dependent DOB + supporting doc (marriage cert or domestic partnership affidavit) when adding spouse. Uploads to benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.example/portal
julia.peopleops: I'll open HRIS ticket with LOA approval, QLE, dependent docs, and payroll journal snippet. Sam - anything else on proration vs catch-up?
samuel.lee: Two options: A) Spread missed premium over remaining pay periods (`spread_over_n_periods`) - smoother cashflow; requires payroll config before cutoff. B) One-time catch-up deduction. Employee preference determines. If spreading, specify `spread_periods` in ticket.
julia.peopleops: I'll ask Maya which she prefers and submit today. Tagging @payroll-bot for required fields.
payroll-bot: Acknowledged. Please include in ticket subject: "M. Torres LOA-return reenroll + payroll catch-up" and fields: `employee_id`, `benefit_code`, `effective_date`, `employee_premium_amount`, `spread_periods` (optional). We'll confirm within 1 business day.
anna.manager: Thanks everyone - Maya will confirm spread vs one-time and I will upload docs now.
julia.peopleops: Great. I'll update the ticket with carrier response and close this thread once processed. :white_check_mark:
